title: A linearly stable excited dark-matter core, proved at nine points: certified spectral stability of the one-node Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson state, and certified brackets of its stability-band edges
description:
In plain words. If dark matter is an ultralight particle, it can settle into a ball held together by its own gravity. The next ball up from the simplest one has a hollow shell inside it, and such balls are usually unstable. A 2024 numerical study (arXiv:2402.07998) found a narrow window of central densities in which the one-shell ball survives every small shake. We prove linear (spectral) stability, with computer-checked error bars, at nine points of the window, and we map and certify where the window ends and how it breaks.

Result A (computer-assisted). At central amplitude sigma0 = 9/5 exactly, the linearised operator J L of the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson system on L^2(R^3) has no spectrum with Re lambda > 0; its spectrum lies on the imaginary axis. The proof certifies the state (E = [-3.10544025447 +/- 3.02e-12]), brackets the Morse indices of L+ (which carries the nonlocal Poisson term) and L- in every angular sector (n(L+) = (2, 1, 1, 0), n(L-) = (1, 1, 1, 0) for L = 0..3, none beyond), certifies a negative-Krein imaginary eigenvalue at L = 0, 1, 2, and closes with a direct Hamiltonian index inequality. A blind float replication from the paper alone reproduced every count and all six Krein frequencies to ten digits (sealed pass rule: relative 1e-4; the ten-digit agreement is a POST HOC observation).

Result B (float map, certified grid and edge brackets). The common stability band is [1.5963117, 1.9841288] (float; bracketed to 1e-7 on the refined grid, base and refined grids agree to 3e-7), narrower than the published 1.55-2.07. Both edges are Krein collisions (our float finding): L = 0 below, L = 2 above (sectors as in Fig. 8 of arXiv:2402.07998). A sealed certified test (all twelve points HOLD) proves linear stability at 1597/1000, 33/20, 17/10, 7/4, 37/20, 19/10, 39/20 and 1983/1000 (nine points with 9/5), and linear instability (a certified growing quartet) at 1595/1000 and 31/20 (L = 0) and at 2 and 1985/1000 (L = 2). The edges therefore lie in certified brackets [1.595, 1.597] and [1.983, 1.985]. The published range contains 1.55 and 2, where the state is now certified unstable; the published band is confirmed in substance and refined in extent.

Not claimed. Nonlinear or orbital stability; uniqueness of the state; stability between the certified points (there the window is a float result); any statement about real halos. To our knowledge (search of arXiv to 16 November, INSPIRE and Zenodo to 17-18 November 2026), this is the first rigorous proof that the first excited (one-node) Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson state is linearly stable at any sigma0.

Checks. Sealed tests, all listed (one duplicate seal VOID); internal hostile referee rounds and an engine audit (internal lab checks, not external peer review); a blind replication; proof checks and a number checker that ties every printed number to its file.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
